```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```



```{r cars}

# ============================================================
# ANALYSE FINANCIERE BANCAIRE - BILANS 2021-2023
# Tableaux, ratios, courbes, barres et diagrammes circulaires
# ============================================================

# 1. Packages -------------------------------------------------

packages <- c(
  "readxl", "dplyr", "tidyr", "stringr",
  "ggplot2", "scales", "openxlsx", "janitor", "purrr"
)

manquants <- packages[
  !vapply(packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(manquants) > 0) {
  install.packages(manquants)
}

invisible(lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE))

# 2. Choisir le fichier Excel -------------------------------

fichier <- file.choose()

feuilles <- readxl::excel_sheets(fichier)

cat("\nFEUILLES DISPONIBLES :\n")
print(feuilles)

banque <- readline(
  "\nSaisis le nom exact de la feuille de la banque à analyser : "
)


```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
